extracted.intended_audience: Toastmasters members preparing to enter the Humorous Speech Contest (club → area → division → district)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing, rehearsing, and delivering a 5–7 minute original humorous speech for Toastmasters contests, including rules, judging criteria, humor techniques, and rehearsal tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length / Timing (contest)
rubrics_metrics.description: 5–7 minutes (plus a 30-second grace period on either end). Timing starts with your first sound or action and ends with your last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay within 5–7 minutes; going under or over (outside the 30-second grace) results in disqualification. Practice with a timer and also with a live audience to learn where adjustments are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: The speech must be substantially original. Quoting others is fine in small doses, but the majority must be your own content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure most material is your own; use quotes sparingly so the speech remains recognizably original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content — Humor as Central but Value Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor must be central, but speeches are judged on value and structure, not just laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft humor that serves a clear message or lesson; judges reward speech value, not only entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be a member in good standing of your club to compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm club membership/status before entering contest levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech Development (25%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scoring dimension (25% of the ballot) rewards clear organization and logical progression — a well-structured story rather than disjointed jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness (25%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also 25% of score; judges assess how well the speech connects with the audience and how clearly the message comes across.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech Value (15%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worth 15% of the score; judges look for speeches that deliver insight, originality, or meaningful contribution beyond just laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery (15%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical presence, body language, eye contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery is 15% of the score and includes stage presence and nonverbal communication that enhances the humor and message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language (10%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language choices should be clear, grammatically appropriate, and suitable for the audience; counted as 10% of the ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of Humor (10%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 10% scoring dimension evaluates whether jokes are appropriate and accessible for the Toastmasters audience; aligns with the 'keep it clean and inclusive' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a Story, Not a String of Jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest is about a humorous speech: a structured story flavored with humor, not stand-up-style punchlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open strong (grab attention with something funny or surprising); build the body (tell a story that naturally creates opportunities for humor); land the ending (tie your story back to a clear message or lesson). Remember judges reward speech value, not just entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Humor Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tested humor techniques such as exaggeration, surprise twists, callbacks, contrast, and physicality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools should always serve your story, not distract from it. Examples: blow everyday situations out of proportion (exaggeration); set up expectations and flip them (surprise); reference an earlier joke for extra laughs (callback); juxtapose serious tone with absurd content (contrast); use gestures and expressions to amplify humor (physicality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep It Clean, Inclusive, and Appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Speeches must be appropriate for all Toastmasters audiences — avoid offensive jokes or stereotypes, inside jokes only a few will get, and language that could alienate or embarrass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winning humorous speeches invite everyone to laugh; be inclusive and avoid material that could alienate or embarrass audience members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice with Pathways (skill-focused rehearsal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Pathways projects as practice opportunities to develop openings, vocal variety, pauses, gestures, and stage presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try humorous openings in Ice Breaker–style speeches; practice vocal variety and pauses in delivery projects; polish gestures and stage presence in body language projects; test entire sections of your contest speech at regular meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic Timing (performance timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pause after punchlines, let laughter land before continuing; rushing kills humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice comedic timing with live audiences; learn where to pause and how long to wait for laughter — timing affects effectiveness and audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest Timing Enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Contest timing is enforced strictly: stay within the 5–7 minute limit (with the 30-second grace) or face disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time your speech during rehearsals and mock performances; adjust content to fit the time window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test and Refine (iteration based on feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use audience reactions as immediate feedback: if people don't laugh where expected, refine the setup or delivery; if they laugh unexpectedly, lean into it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice in front of club members, family, and friends; track what works and iterate — winning speeches are crafted through iteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close with Heart / Takeaway
rubrics_metrics.description: End with a clear takeaway — a moral, reflection, or lesson — so the speech leaves the audience with something to think about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for speech value; a laugh tied to insight is more memorable than laughter without meaning.
